- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is positive but recent history shows mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ prices unless sentiment strongly signals reversal.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; anchor forecast to 30-day moving average unless sentiment shifts.
